cost_basis.disclaimer: Rounded COOLSPOT screening allowances for comparing portfolios; these are not contractor quotes, bids, or construction estimates.
shared_exclusions: Property acquisition, major utility relocation, environmental review, and unusual site remediation
Future inflation, procurement escalation, and costs identified by engineering design
Benefits or costs outside the stated planning unit

interventions.label: Shade structure
interventions.description: A fixed shelter or shade structure sized for a transit waiting area.

applicability.screening_rule: Screen only published transit-stop locations; do not infer that an existing stop is unshaded.
preconstruction_checks: Verify existing shade throughout operating hours and seasons
Confirm agency ownership, permits, ADA clear path, boarding clearance, utilities, drainage, visibility, and crash safety
Select orientation and dimensions using a site-specific solar and rider-use assessment
applicability.exclusion_rule: Exclude a site when adequate shade already exists or clearance, ownership, safety, or constructability cannot be confirmed.

planning_cost.basis: The estimate anchors to LADOT's approximate traditional-shelter installation figure; the internal range allows for design and site variability without representing a bid.

benefit_evidence.qualitative_benefit: Well-oriented shade reduces direct solar exposure for people waiting at a transit stop and can improve outdoor thermal comfort.
benefit_evidence.transfer_limit: The catalog does not assign a temperature reduction because actual coverage depends on sun angle, orientation, materials, weather, and how riders use the stop.

uncertainty.summary: A mapped Metro stop establishes a waiting location, not existing shade, available right-of-way, or shelter feasibility.
factors: Existing tree, building, or shelter shade is absent from the MVP data
Solar orientation and useful shade coverage are site and time dependent
Permitting, utilities, ADA clearance, drainage, and ownership can materially change cost or feasibility

lifespan_maintenance.expected_lifespan: Not established by the cited local planning sources; determine during design and procurement.
lifespan_maintenance.maintenance_note: Budget for inspection, cleaning, graffiti removal, lighting or panel repair where fitted, and eventual component replacement.

interventions.label: Tree canopy
interventions.description: A planning package of approximately ten climate-appropriate shade trees at a public school or park site.

applicability.screening_rule: Screen mapped public school and park sites as potential hosts; a site record does not prove planting space or low canopy.
preconstruction_checks: Verify ownership approval, existing canopy, planting space, soil volume, species suitability, irrigation, utilities, and accessible clearances
Confirm a funded five-year establishment and replacement plan
Use a qualified arborist and the applicable agency planting standards
applicability.exclusion_rule: Exclude sites without verified planting space, establishment water, responsible maintenance, or safe utility and infrastructure clearance.

planning_cost.basis: The City published a $2,375 planting-and-three-year-watering baseline per 24-inch-box tree in 2016. COOLSPOT rounds to $5,000 per tree for a ten-tree package to include screening, five-year establishment care, replacement risk, and contingency; current site design and bids are still required.

benefit_evidence.qualitative_benefit: Established trees can cool public space through shade and evapotranspiration while providing additional environmental co-benefits.
benefit_evidence.transfer_limit: No near-term temperature effect is assigned because cooling depends on survival, species, maturity, irrigation, placement, weather, and surrounding urban form.

uncertainty.summary: The MVP has authoritative site locations but no tree inventory, canopy-gap layer, soil assessment, utility survey, irrigation plan, or survival forecast.
factors: Young trees need years of successful establishment before providing mature shade
Drought, heat, pests, species choice, soil volume, and watering affect survival and growth
Existing canopy and underground or overhead conflicts are not represented

lifespan_maintenance.expected_lifespan: Potentially multi-decade, but no lifespan is assumed for scoring because survival and species are unknown.
lifespan_maintenance.maintenance_note: Los Angeles requires a five-year establishment commitment for new public-right-of-way trees; ongoing watering, inspection, pruning, pest response, and replacement remain necessary.

interventions.label: Cool pavement
interventions.description: A reflective pavement treatment for a verified, suitable public paved surface or corridor segment.

applicability.screening_rule: Require direct evidence of a public paved treatment area; a nearby school, park, or hot tile alone is not pavement evidence.
preconstruction_checks: Verify ownership, surface material and condition, treatment area, traffic plan, wet traction, drainage, glare, accessibility, and product compatibility
Evaluate pedestrian radiant exposure and complementary shade for the proposed design
Confirm product durability, reapplication plan, and life-cycle impacts
applicability.exclusion_rule: Exclude sites lacking verified public pavement geometry or with unresolved traction, glare, surface-condition, pedestrian-comfort, or maintenance concerns.

planning_cost.basis: Los Angeles appropriated $191,000 for fifteen one-block cool-pavement installations in FY 2016-17 and later installed 10–12-block Pacoima projects without publishing site-level prices. This conservative package allowance covers preparation, coating, mobilization, traffic control, design, and contingency; it is not a current product quote.

benefit_evidence.qualitative_benefit: A year-long Pacoima field study found predominantly beneficial but variable changes in pavement surface temperature, near-surface air temperature, and thermal-comfort indicators.
benefit_evidence.transfer_limit: No study value is applied as a forecast; effects varied with coating properties, weather, surroundings, spatial scale, and comparison method, and other studies have raised pedestrian radiant-exposure concerns.

uncertainty.summary: Pacoima evidence is locally relevant, but the MVP lacks verified pavement area, material, condition, albedo, pedestrian geometry, product choice, and life-cycle data.
factors: Observed cooling varied across locations, times, weather, and analytical comparisons
Reflective short-wave exposure can affect pedestrian comfort depending on context
Product durability, replacement interval, and life-cycle impacts require project-specific evidence

lifespan_maintenance.expected_lifespan: Unknown for the proposed site and product; the cited City report did not establish a public-street replacement cycle.
lifespan_maintenance.maintenance_note: Inspect wet traction, coating wear, soiling, glare, drainage, and thermal performance, and fund reapplication only after product-specific design review.
